---
title: "Performance"
---

phplyr's functions call one or two methods of the table they are given, so
the backend determines how fast a pipeline runs. These timings cover the
workloads and machines below.

## Methods

Both benchmark sets ran on 2026-11-01 on an Apple M5 Ultra with PHP 8.5.10,
phibble 0.6.0, and phpolars 0.2.1 (Polars 0.55.2, two threads). DataFrame and
SQLite run single-threaded.

| | phibble workloads | Backend pipelines |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Script | `bench/harness.php` | `bench/backends.php`, and `bench/backends.R` for dplyr 1.2.1 |
| Data | `bench/generate.php`, with phibble's generator and seed. `events.csv`: 1,000,000 rows of `id`, `key` (10,000 values), `g` (8 labels), `x` (float, about 2% NA), and `t` (datetime). `dims.csv`: 100,000 rows of `key`, `label`, and `w`. | `sales`: 1,000,000 rows, with no date or datetime columns. `stores`: 100 rows. |
| Backends | DataFrame, SQLite, and PolarsTable, each as a phplyr pipeline and as direct table calls | DataFrame, PolarsTable, SQLite, and dplyr |
| Statistic | Median of three runs | Best of three runs |
| Timer | Through `collect()`; loading the data is not timed | Through `collect()`; loading the data is not timed |

```bash
php bench/generate.php 1000000
php bench/harness.php --backend=dataframe --runs=3
php bench/harness.php --backend=sqlite --runs=3
php -d extension=php_polars bench/harness.php --backend=polars --runs=3
php -d extension=php_polars bench/backends.php --csv-dir=bench/data
Rscript bench/backends.R
```

## phplyr's overhead

The phplyr pipeline and the same calls made directly on the table differed
in both directions, by at most 13% at 1,000,000 rows. At 100,000 rows, the
largest difference was 16 ms. Grouped slices, `pivot_*()`, and `complete()`
build on the same table methods.

## phibble workloads at 1,000,000 rows

| Workload | DataFrame (s) | SQLite (s) | PolarsTable (s) |
| --- | --: | --: | --: |
| Grouped `summarise()` of `n()`, `mean()`, and `sum()` by `key` | 0.17 | 0.61 | 0.02 |
| The same with closures | 0.40 | 2.02 | 0.62 |
| Grouped `arrange(t)`, then `mutate()` with `lag()`, `cumsum()`, and `row_number()` | 0.94 | 5.44 | 0.38 |
| `filter(col('x')->gt(0)->and(...))` | 0.13 | 0.38 | 0.04 |
| The same filter as a closure | 0.85 | 2.58 | 1.09 |
| `mutate()` with two expressions | 0.24 | 1.90 | 0.29 |
| `left_join()` of 1M × 100k rows on `key` | 0.25 | 2.83 | 0.39 |
| `arrange(desc('x'), 'id')` | 0.74 | 2.10 | 0.37 |

DataFrame peaked at about 1.3 GB of memory for the 1M-row table and its
results.

## Choosing a backend

- **In-memory `DataFrame`** suits data that fits in memory. In the grouped
  summary above, expression arguments took 0.17 s and closures 0.40 s,
  because phibble computes expressions in one pass without building a table
  per group.
- **A database table (`Phibble\tbl()`)** avoids loading the data into PHP.
  With expressions, `filter()` and `summarise()` run in the database, and only
  the result reaches PHP. These timings exclude loading the data.
- **Pipelines that return every row** (`mutate()`, `arrange()`, unfiltered
  joins) spend most of their database time transferring rows to PHP.
- **Closures on a database table** load all rows first and then run in
  memory. Use `col()` expressions and phplyr's helpers to keep the work in
  SQL.
- **SQLite columns need declared types.** PDO binds values as strings. In an
  untyped column, SQLite stores them as text and compares numbers as text.
- **PolarsTable** (phibble's Polars backend, on the phpolars extension) runs
  expressions in Polars. A closure step converts the data to a DataFrame and
  back, so the closure workloads above were slower on PolarsTable than on
  DataFrame.

## Backend pipelines

`bench/backends.php` times three phplyr pipelines and checks that DataFrame,
PolarsTable, and SQLite return the same rows. It is adapted from phpolars'
benchmark script. `bench/backends.R` runs pipelines A and B with dplyr and
checks that its row counts and column sums match phplyr's.

- **A:** filter, join a store lookup, two-key summarise, then a ranking window.
- **B:** grouped `lag(orderBy:)`, `cumsum()`, and a share of the group total
  over all rows.
- **C:** pipeline A with a closure in `filter()`. It has no dplyr version,
  because its closure is PHP code.

| Pipeline, 1M rows | DataFrame (s) | PolarsTable (s) | SQLite (s) | dplyr (s) |
| --- | --: | --: | --: | --: |
| A: reduce to a ranked summary | 0.62 | 0.08 | 0.54 | 0.08 |
| B: windows over every row | 1.58 | 0.39 | 3.85 | 0.02 |
| C: A with a closure | 1.17 | 0.91 | 2.08 | |

The full results, with every repeat and version, are in
[`benchmarks/backends-results.json`](benchmarks/backends-results.json) and
[`benchmarks/dplyr-results.json`](benchmarks/dplyr-results.json).

PolarsTable's cost outside Polars is converting results to PHP values and
running closure steps. Measured separately on the 1M-row `events.csv`, best of
three:

- Collecting four plain columns took 0.15 s, and the datetime column `t` added
  about 0.01 s.
- A closure in `filter()` took 0.88 s, most of it converting the data to a
  DataFrame and back.

PolarsTable suits pipelines written in expressions, especially ones that
reduce the data before collecting, and data that starts in Polars:
`PolarsTable::fromPolars(Phpolars\read_csv($path))` skips phibble's CSV
parse.
